description.narrative:
The overall goal of the programme is to Advance Inclusive Governance, Empowerment, and Resilience of Communities Towards the Realisation of Human Rights in Kenya.
The overall objective is to Enhance Agency of Rights Holders and Responsiveness of Duty Bearers in Defending and Upholding Human Rights.
The strategic programmatic niche is within the following key results areas:
Results Area 1 - Inclusive Governance & Democracy aims to strengthen community voice and agency in building responsive and accountable governance structures and processes.
Expected outcomes under Result Area 1:
(i) strengthening community voices in decision-making and development processes; (ii) increasing the capacity of the communities to demand and claim human rights, and (iii) Enhanced accountability by duty bearers toward responsible service delivery.
Results Area 2 - Community Empowerment, Resilience & Adaptation aims to improve the resilience, and adaptative capacity of the community to environmental, and socio-economic disruptions.
Expected outcomed under Result Area 2:
i) Enhance adaptive capacities of communities to cope with the effects of climate change and other shocks from unprecedented disasters, and ii) Enhance capacity of the community to adapt to socioeconomic shocks
Result Area 3 - Gender Equality aims to strengthen gender agency in society
Expected outcome under Result Area 3:
(i) Enhanced resilience against gender-based violence ii) Increased political inclusion and participation of women in political processes, and iii) Enhanced equitable and non-discriminative enjoyment of Sexual and Reproductive Health Rights.
Result Area 4 - Networking, Linkages, and Movement Building aims to empower partnerships, networks, coalitions, and movements for sustained aggregate voice and action
Expected outcome under Result Area 4:
i) Strengthening effective citizen partnerships, networks, coalitions, and sustained movements, ii) coalescing voices and collective action toward strategic solidarity, iii) Enhanced strategic results communications, documentation, and dissemination of programme impacts and emerging insights, and iv) Strengthened leadership, foresight, and organisational sustainability.
Result Area 5 - Capacity Development aims to strengthen the internal capacity of ForumCiv and its partners to deliver on their mandate
Expected outcome under Result Area 5:
i) WWP III stakeholders strengthening organisational, programmatic, and thematic capacity, ii) Enhanced intergenerational mentorship and experiential learning for young men and women towards effective change-making and leadership, and iii) Partner organisations are more sustainable.

Wajibu Wetu Program III (WWP III) syftar till att främja inkluderande styrning, bemyndigande och motståndskraft för samhällen mot förverkligandet av deras mänskliga rättigheter. De centrala teman för programmet är innovation och motståndskraft och ForumCiv fokuserar på att bygga starkare samhällen genom strategiska civilsamhällespartnerskap; adresserar ekonomisk, miljömässig och social motståndskraft ur ett människorättsperspektiv; stärka rörelsebyggande genom en robust kapacitetsutvecklingsstrategi och främja hållbara strategier. Programmets mål kommer att uppnås genom fem resultatområden: 1) Stärka inkluderande styrning och demokrati; 2) Förbättra samhällets egenmakt, motståndskraft och anpassning; 3) Bidra till jämställdhet; 4) Nätverk, kopplingar och rörelsebyggande, och 5) Förbättra kapaciteten hos civilsamhällsaktörer Tillvägagångssätten för genomförandet är: vidareförmedlande av medel till lokala organisationer genom flexibla, innovativa och behovsstyrda bidrag; strategiska partnerskap - förtroendebaserade partnerskap med delade värderingar; innovativ kapacitetsutveckling driven av ett ramverk för bemyndigande, och nätverk, länkar och byggande av rörelser. Wajibu Wetu betyder Vårt ansvar och programmet bygger på resultat som gjorts under de två föregående faserna.

Wajibu Wetu Programme III (WWP III) aims to Advance Inclusive Governance, Empowerment, and Resilience of Communities Towards the Realization of their Human Rights. The central themes for the program are innovativeness and resilience and ForumCiv focuses on building stronger communities through strategic civil society partnerships, addressing resilience economically, environmentally and socially from a human rights perspective, strengthening movement building through a robust capacity development approach and promoting sustainable strategies. The programme goal will be achieved through five results areas: 1) Strengthening Inclusive Governance and Democracy; 2) Enhancing Community Empowerment, Resilience, and Adaptation; 3) Contributing to Gender Equality; 4) Networking, Linkages and Movement Building, and 5) Enhancing Capacities of CSOs. The implementation approaches are: sub-granting through flexibility, innovative and needs-driven grant making; strategic partnerships - trust-based partnerships aligned shared values; innovative capacity development driven by an empowerment framework, and; networking, linkages and movement building. Wajibu Wetu means Our Responsibility and the programme builds on gains made in the previous two phases.

description.narrative:
During the fiscal year 2024 (January to December 2024), the Wajibu Wetu III programme realized tramendous achievements in all the result areas. The achievements are summarized below.
Result area 1: Inclusive Governance and Democracy: The programme curated and organized regional dialogue platforms christened Jumuika Sikika Mtaani in the Nyanza Region and Wajir Counties, bringing together duty bearers and rights holders. These dialogue platforms were to augment the conversations during the International Day of Democracy (IDD) and the Annual Democracy and Human Rights Festival (ADHRF), both which were aimed at strengthening community voice and agency to promote inclusive governance and democracy. Similarly, the programme witnessed successful youth-led initiatives in Kilifi, Mombasa and Kakamega counties that have contributed to improved service delivery, such as the inclusion of 8 community proposed projects such as the construction of Mirere Primary school classes and staff rooms, rehabilitation of dilapidated classrooms at Mukhonje Primary School, and revival of construction work at Kithengwani and Mrima Mkulu dispensaries.
Result area 2: Community Empowerment, Resilience and Adaptation: ForumCiv in collaboration with other partners carried out initiatives that enhance community resilience and adaptation to negative shocks of climate change. For instance, through a partnership with the Consortium of Disabled Persons Organisation in Kenya, Isiolo Gender Watch and the Horn of Africa Institute curated and organized a celebration to mark the World Environment Day in Kajiado and Isiolo counties respectively under the theme Land Restoration, Desertification and Drought Resilience. One of the key results from the conversation in Kajiado was enhanced relationships with the Kajiado County government, with an intention for members of CDPOK benefit from the World Bank- funded FLLoCA project by having their members represented in the Ward Climate Council. Besides this WW:JS! Programme held a capacity exchange session with the WW:JS! Programme partners on the Intersection of Gender and Climate Change and International Diplomacy and Negotiations on Climate Change, a peer exposure visits for the 11 partners delivering on the climate justice thematic area and various intersections, as well as participating in the COP29 session in Azerbaijan thus enhancing ForumCivs engagement at the international policy level. COP29 helped establish ForumCiv as a climate justice and environment convener, bringing together African CSOs and NGOs working in the space.
Result area 3: Gender Equality: ForumCiv in collaboration with partner organisations that are women led and gender-equality focused such as CREAW, CWID, RONA and Talanta Africa advocated for an end to GBV and femicide in the country. The advocacy campaign with hashtags #EndFemicide Campaign and #DarkValentine resulted in the Directorate of Criminal Investigation putting up a special hotline number for reporting of cases as well as a special team to investigate femicides cases. The campaigns got a further boost when the Chief Justice of the Republic of Kenya undertook to ensure that there are courts handling trauma-informed sexual and gender-based violence cases. Besides this, the programme also held a training for 34 partners and staff on Gender Equality in Nairobi. The capacity exchange session highlighted areas such as Gender Mainstreaming, GBV and Gender Focused Budgeting. As a result of the training, partners undertook to re-evaluate the gender responsiveness of their respective projects and organizations.
Result area 4: Networking, linkages, and movement building, and Capacity Development: The WW:JS! Programme developed platforms that encourage the unification of voices and the establishment of movements. Mos of the partners utilized these platforms during the period to create coalitions and networks aimed at strengthening their initiatives. For instance, the capacity-building opportunities offered, including the CEOs Forum have improved organizational visibility and enabled partners, such as CREAW, to engage in prestigious events like the Seventh Annual Scientific Conference on Sexual and Reproductive Health Rights (SRHR).
